moTa: Bản rút gọn kiểu IELTS Academic: Listening 20 câu (thuê xe ô tô · hai sinh viên bàn bài thuyết trình) + Reading 20 câu (nuôi ong trong thành phố · tuần làm việc bốn ngày).

nhom.huongDan: Part 1 — Câu 1–10. Nghe cuộc gọi thuê xe ô tô và điền vào phiếu đặt xe. Mỗi chỗ trống viết MỘT TỪ hoặc MỘT SỐ. Chỉ nghe MỘT lần.

nghe.t: Good afternoon, Coastline Car Hire. This is Owen. How can I help?
Hi. I'm flying in next month and I'd like to rent a car for a few days.
Certainly. Let me open a new booking. Can I start with your family name?
It's Brennick. B, R, E, double N, I, C, K.
Thank you, Ms Brennick. And which country is your driving licence from?
It's from Canada. I live in the United States now, but I've never changed it.
No problem, a Canadian licence is fine. When would you like to collect the car?
I land on Friday evening, but I'll be tired, so I'd rather pick it up on Saturday morning.
Saturday it is. And how many days do you need it for?
I was thinking of a week, but that's probably too long. Let's say five days.
Five days. Now, what kind of car are you looking for? Our small cars are the cheapest.
There are four of us, with a lot of luggage. I think we need a medium one.
A medium car, then. Those are forty-six pounds a day. The small ones are thirty-eight, but I agree, you'd find it hard to fit the bags in.
Forty-six is OK. Does the price include insurance?
Basic insurance is included. If anything is damaged, though, you would pay the first five hundred pounds. For a little extra you can bring that down to zero.
I'll keep the basic one, thanks. What about extras? My son is three.
Then by law he'll need a child seat. We can fit one for you, free of charge.
Great. And I don't need a map system, I'll use my phone.
Fine. Where would you like to collect the car? We have a desk at the airport and an office beside the station in the city centre.
We're staying in town on Friday night, so the station would be more convenient.
The station office, good. It opens at eight thirty. One more thing: the car comes with a full tank, and we ask you to bring it back full. If not, we charge for the fuel.
Understood. Do you need a deposit today?
Just a small one, twenty pounds, and that comes off the final bill. And how would you like to receive the confirmation? By text message or email?
Email, please. I don't have a local phone number yet.
Email it is. Let me take your card details.

cau.de:
COASTLINE CAR HIRE — Booking form
Family name: ___
cau.giaiThich: 'It's Brennick. B, R, E, double N, I, C, K.' double N = hai chữ N liền nhau (NN) — cách đánh vần rất hay gặp trong Part 1.

cau.de: Driving licence issued in: ___
cau.giaiThich: 'It's from Canada. I live in the United States now, but I've never changed it.' Bẫy: nơi đang sống (United States) khác nơi cấp bằng lái (Canada).

cau.de: Collection day: ___
cau.giaiThich: 'I land on Friday evening, but I'll be tired, so I'd rather pick it up on Saturday morning.' Friday là ngày hạ cánh; pick up = collect (nhận xe) là thứ Bảy.

cau.de: Length of hire: ___ days
cau.giaiThich: 'I was thinking of a week, but that's probably too long. Let's say five days.' Một tuần là ý ban đầu đã bị chính người nói gạt đi.

cau.de: Size of car: ___
cau.giaiThich: 'There are four of us, with a lot of luggage. I think we need a medium one.' Nhân viên gợi ý xe small (rẻ nhất) nhưng khách chọn medium (cỡ vừa).

cau.de: Cost per day: £ ___
cau.giaiThich: 'A medium car, then. Those are forty-six pounds a day. The small ones are thirty-eight.' 38 là giá xe nhỏ (bẫy); khách xác nhận 'Forty-six is OK'.

cau.de: Extra equipment: a child ___ (no charge)
cau.giaiThich: 'by law he'll need a child seat. We can fit one for you, free of charge.' free of charge = no charge. Hệ thống bản đồ bị khách từ chối nên không phải đáp án.

cau.de: Collect from: the office next to the ___
cau.giaiThich: 'a desk at the airport and an office beside the station' rồi khách chọn 'the station would be more convenient'. beside = next to; airport là bẫy.

cau.de: Return the car with a full ___
cau.giaiThich: 'the car comes with a full tank, and we ask you to bring it back full. If not, we charge for the fuel.' tank = bình xăng; bring back = return.

cau.de: Deposit paid today: £ ___
cau.giaiThich: 'Just a small one, twenty pounds, and that comes off the final bill.' Đừng nhầm với five hundred pounds — đó là khoản khách phải chịu nếu xe hư hỏng.

nhom.huongDan: Part 2 — Câu 11–20. Nghe hai sinh viên Hana và Leo bàn về bài thuyết trình môn Môi trường và chọn A, B hoặc C. Chỉ nghe MỘT lần.

nghe.t: Hi Leo. Have you got a few minutes to talk about the recycling project? The presentation is only two weeks away.
Sure. I've been looking at the survey results all morning. We got a hundred and forty replies, which is more than I expected.
Me too. I thought we'd be lucky to reach a hundred. Why do you think so many people answered?
Well, I'd like to say it was our clever poster, but honestly, I think it's because the survey was so short. It took two minutes on a phone.
That's true. So, what stands out in the results?
Almost everyone says recycling matters to them. But when we asked what they actually do, fewer than half sort their rubbish every day.
Did they say why not? I assumed people were just lazy.
A few admitted that. But the most common reason was that they weren't sure which bin to use. The labels in the halls of residence are really confusing.
Interesting. That fits with what Doctor Malik said in the lecture, that information is a bigger problem than attitude.
Exactly. So I think that should be the main message of our talk.
Agreed. Now, how are we going to present the numbers? I started making a table last night.
Hmm. A table is accurate, but people can't read it from the back of the room. I'd prefer bar charts, one for each question.
Fine, bar charts. I'll throw my table away. What about the interviews? We planned to do ten, and we've only done six.
I know. But the six we have are really detailed. I don't think more interviews would tell us anything new. I'd rather spend the time on analysing them properly.
OK, but then we must explain that in the talk, so nobody thinks we were careless.
Good point. Now, the photos. I took some pictures of the bins in my hall, with rubbish in the wrong places.
Can we use those? Do we need permission?
There are no people in them, so the tutor said it's fine. We just have to say where they were taken.
Great. What about the ending? I think we should finish with a recommendation, not just a summary.
Yes. My idea was to suggest that the university gives a prize to the hall that recycles most.
Hmm. Competitions are fun, but they don't last. Our own results point to something simpler: clearer labels on the bins, with pictures.
You're right, that follows directly from the data. Let's recommend that.
So, who does what? I'm happy to make the slides, because I've already got the software.
Then I'll write the script for both of us. And I'll email Doctor Malik to check how long we've got. I think it's ten minutes, but some groups were told fifteen.
Please do. If it's only ten, we'll have to cut the section on interviews.
Let's not decide until we hear from him. Shall we meet again on Thursday, after the seminar?
Thursday's good. I'll bring a first version of the slides.

cau.de: Leo believes that many students replied to the survey because
luaChon: the poster advertising it was attractive.
it could be completed very quickly.
students care a great deal about recycling.
cau.giaiThich: 'I'd like to say it was our clever poster, but honestly, I think it's because the survey was so short. It took two minutes.' so short = completed very quickly. Poster bị gạt bằng 'but honestly'.

cau.de: What do the results show about students' behaviour?
luaChon: Most students recycle every day.
The majority think recycling is unimportant.
Under fifty per cent separate their waste daily.
cau.giaiThich: 'fewer than half sort their rubbish every day.' fewer than half = under fifty per cent; sort rubbish = separate waste. B ngược bài: gần như ai cũng nói tái chế quan trọng.

cau.de: The main reason students gave for not recycling was that
luaChon: they did not know which bin was the right one.
they could not be bothered to do it.
the bins were too far from their rooms.
cau.giaiThich: 'the most common reason was that they weren't sure which bin to use.' most common = main. Lười ('lazy') chỉ là phỏng đoán của Hana và 'A few admitted that' — số ít, không phải lý do chính.

cau.de: How will the students show their figures in the presentation?
luaChon: in a series of bar charts
in one large table
on a printed handout
cau.giaiThich: 'I'd prefer bar charts, one for each question.' — 'Fine, bar charts. I'll throw my table away.' Bảng (table) là ý ban đầu của Hana nhưng bị bỏ vì ngồi cuối phòng không đọc được.

cau.de: Why does Leo not want to do any more interviews?
luaChon: There is no time left before the presentation.
The existing ones already provide enough information.
Students are unwilling to be interviewed.
cau.giaiThich: 'the six we have are really detailed. I don't think more interviews would tell us anything new.' Tức là sáu bài đã đủ thông tin. Anh ấy nói muốn DÙNG thời gian để phân tích, không nói hết thời gian.

cau.de: What must the students do in order to use Leo's photographs?
luaChon: ask the people in them for permission
get permission from the hall manager
state the place where they were taken
cau.giaiThich: 'There are no people in them, so the tutor said it's fine. We just have to say where they were taken.' say where = state the place. Ảnh không có người nên không cần xin phép ai.

cau.de: What recommendation will they make at the end of the talk?
luaChon: a recycling competition between halls
more bins in every hall
labels that are easier to understand
cau.giaiThich: 'Our own results point to something simpler: clearer labels on the bins, with pictures.' — 'Let's recommend that.' clearer = easier to understand. Cuộc thi có thưởng là ý của Leo, bị bác vì 'they don't last'.

cau.de: Hana will prepare the slides because
luaChon: she already has the program that is needed.
she is better at design than Leo.
Leo is busy finishing the table.
cau.giaiThich: 'I'm happy to make the slides, because I've already got the software.' software = program. Hai phương án còn lại không được nói tới (bảng đã bị bỏ từ trước).

cau.de: Leo is going to contact Doctor Malik in order to
luaChon: ask for extra time to finish the project.
confirm the length of the presentation.
send him the script to check.
cau.giaiThich: 'I'll email Doctor Malik to check how long we've got. I think it's ten minutes, but some groups were told fifteen.' check how long = confirm the length. Leo viết kịch bản nhưng không nói sẽ gửi cho thầy.

cau.de: What will the students decide after they hear from Doctor Malik?
luaChon: when to hold their next meeting
which of them will speak first
whether to leave out the part about interviews
cau.giaiThich: 'If it's only ten, we'll have to cut the section on interviews.' — 'Let's not decide until we hear from him.' cut the section = leave out the part. Buổi gặp thứ Năm đã chốt luôn, không phải chờ.

nhom.huongDan: Passage 1 — Câu 21–30. Câu 21–24: True / False / Not Given. Câu 25–27: chọn A–D. Câu 28–30: điền MỘT TỪ lấy nguyên văn từ bài đọc.
nhom.doan:
BEES IN THE CITY

A  On the roof of an office block, twenty floors above a busy road, a woman in a white suit lifts the lid from a wooden box. Inside are around forty thousand honeybees. Scenes like this have become common in cities around the world over the past two decades, as hotels, banks and schools have installed hives on their roofs. Urban beekeeping, once an unusual hobby, is now fashionable.

B  It may seem surprising that bees can live well among concrete and traffic, but cities offer them several advantages. Parks, gardens and balconies contain a wide variety of plants, and because these are chosen to look attractive in different seasons, something is in flower for most of the year. Farmland, by contrast, is often covered by a single crop that blooms for only a few weeks. In addition, city gardeners generally use fewer chemicals than farmers do. As a result, urban hives frequently produce more honey than those in the countryside.

C  The fashion began with good intentions. News reports about falling bee numbers persuaded many people that keeping a hive was a way to help nature. However, scientists who study insects point out a misunderstanding here. The honeybee is only one of more than twenty thousand species of bee, and it is not in danger: it is kept by humans in huge numbers, rather like chickens. The bees that are really at risk are wild ones. Most of these live alone instead of in large colonies, make no honey, and nest in holes in the ground or in dead wood.

D  In fact, too many hives may make life harder for wild bees. A single colony collects an enormous quantity of pollen during the summer, and when hives are placed close together, less is left for other insects. Researchers in several European cities have reported that fewer wild bees are found in areas where the number of hives has grown rapidly. Some city councils have reacted by limiting new hives, particularly in districts with little green space.

E  None of this means that city residents cannot help. Experts say that the most useful action is simply to grow more flowers, especially native plants, and to choose kinds that bloom at different times. Leaving a corner of the garden untidy, with some bare soil and old stems, gives wild bees somewhere to nest. Such steps are less exciting than producing a jar of rooftop honey, but they benefit hundreds of species instead of one.

cau.de: The woman described in paragraph A is employed by the owners of the office block.
luaChon: True
False
Not Given
cau.giaiThich: Đoạn A chỉ tả một phụ nữ mặc đồ trắng mở thùng ong trên mái toà nhà, không nói bà làm việc cho ai ⇒ Not Given. Đừng tự suy diễn từ bối cảnh.

cau.de: Plants in cities usually flower over a shorter period than crops on farms.
luaChon: True
False
Not Given
cau.giaiThich: Đoạn B: ở thành phố 'something is in flower for most of the year', còn nông trại 'a single crop that blooms for only a few weeks'. Câu hỏi nói ngược lại ⇒ False.

cau.de: People who garden in cities tend to use smaller amounts of chemicals than farmers.
luaChon: True
False
Not Given
cau.giaiThich: Đoạn B: 'city gardeners generally use fewer chemicals than farmers do.' generally = tend to; fewer = smaller amounts of ⇒ True.

cau.de: Most kinds of wild bee do not live in colonies.
luaChon: True
False
Not Given
cau.giaiThich: Đoạn C: 'Most of these live alone instead of in large colonies.' live alone instead of in colonies = do not live in colonies ⇒ True.

cau.de: According to paragraph B, why do urban hives often produce more honey?
luaChon: Cities are warmer than the countryside.
City bees do not need to fly as far.
A greater range of plants is in flower through the year.
Urban beekeepers have had better training.
cau.giaiThich: Đoạn B: 'a wide variety of plants … something is in flower for most of the year … As a result, urban hives frequently produce more honey.' wide variety = greater range. Nhiệt độ, quãng bay, đào tạo đều không được nhắc.

cau.de: What mistake do many new beekeepers make, according to paragraph C?
luaChon: They believe that honeybees usually live alone.
They think that keeping honeybees protects the bees most at risk.
They expect a hive to produce honey straight away.
They do not realise how many bees a hive contains.
cau.giaiThich: Đoạn C: nhiều người tin nuôi ong mật là giúp thiên nhiên, nhưng ong mật 'is not in danger'; 'The bees that are really at risk are wild ones.' Đó chính là 'misunderstanding'. A lấy chi tiết của ong hoang gán sang ong mật.

cau.de: Why have some city councils restricted the number of new hives?
luaChon: Residents complained about being stung.
Rooftop hives were damaging buildings.
Too much honey was being sold locally.
Large numbers of honeybees leave less food for wild bees.
cau.giaiThich: Đoạn D: 'when hives are placed close together, less is left for other insects' và ong hoang ít đi ở nơi số thùng ong tăng nhanh ⇒ 'councils have reacted by limiting new hives'. limiting = restricted. A, B, C không có trong bài.

cau.de: The writer says honeybees are kept in very large numbers, in a similar way to ___.
cau.giaiThich: Đoạn C: 'it is kept by humans in huge numbers, rather like chickens.' rather like = in a similar way to; huge = very large.

cau.de: Wild bees may make their nests underground or in dead ___.
cau.giaiThich: Đoạn C: 'nest in holes in the ground or in dead wood.' in holes in the ground = underground. Không điền stems: 'old stems' ở đoạn E đi với old, không phải dead.

cau.de: Experts recommend growing more flowers, and ___ plants in particular.
cau.giaiThich: Đoạn E: 'grow more flowers, especially native plants.' especially = in particular. native = bản địa.

nhom.huongDan: Passage 2 — Câu 31–40. Câu 31–34: True / False / Not Given. Câu 35–37: chọn A–D. Câu 38–40: điền MỘT TỪ lấy nguyên văn từ bài đọc.
nhom.doan:
THE FOUR-DAY WEEK

A  When the American car maker Henry Ford gave his factory workers a five-day week in 1926, many business leaders thought he had made a serious mistake. Within a few decades, however, the two-day weekend had become normal in much of the world. Almost a century later, a similar argument is taking place about whether the working week should be cut again, this time to four days.

B  The idea is usually tested in a particular form: staff work around thirty-two hours instead of forty, but receive the same pay, and in return they are expected to produce the same amount as before. In one large trial in Britain in 2022, about sixty companies followed this model for six months. When it ended, most of them decided to continue. Managers reported that income had not fallen, and far fewer employees had left their jobs during the trial than in a normal period.

C  How can people do the same work in less time? Those who took part gave similar answers. Meetings were made shorter or cancelled, and some firms introduced quiet hours in which nobody could be interrupted. Workers also said that, knowing they had a free day ahead, they wasted less time. Supporters argue that long hours have never guaranteed good results; tired people make more mistakes and are ill more often.

D  Critics are not convinced. They note that the companies in such trials chose to take part, so they were probably the ones most likely to succeed. Most were offices in fields such as marketing and software, where work can be reorganised fairly easily. A hospital or a restaurant cannot simply close for an extra day, and would need to hire more staff to cover the hours, which raises costs. There is also the risk that four days become more intense, with employees feeling under greater pressure to finish everything.

E  For this reason, some organisations have chosen different versions of the idea. One is to keep five days but shorten each of them. This suits parents, who can collect their children from school. Another is to give the extra day off only during the quieter months of the year. What the experiments have shown most clearly is that there is no single answer. The best arrangement depends on the kind of work that is being done, and on what workers themselves want from their free time.

cau.de: Other business leaders welcomed Henry Ford's decision when he made it.
luaChon: True
False
Not Given
cau.giaiThich: Đoạn A: 'many business leaders thought he had made a serious mistake.' Cho là sai lầm nghiêm trọng thì không thể là hoan nghênh (welcomed) ⇒ False.

cau.de: Ford's company made higher profits after it introduced the five-day week.
luaChon: True
False
Not Given
cau.giaiThich: Đoạn A chỉ nói Ford cho công nhân làm 5 ngày và sau này cuối tuần hai ngày thành bình thường; không có thông tin nào về lợi nhuận của công ty ⇒ Not Given.

cau.de: Staff in the trial model are paid as much as they were before.
luaChon: True
False
Not Given
cau.giaiThich: Đoạn B: 'staff work around thirty-two hours instead of forty, but receive the same pay.' the same pay = paid as much as before ⇒ True.

cau.de: Most companies went back to a five-day week when the British trial finished.
luaChon: True
False
Not Given
cau.giaiThich: Đoạn B: 'When it ended, most of them decided to continue.' Đa số tiếp tục tuần bốn ngày chứ không quay lại năm ngày ⇒ False.

cau.de: According to paragraph C, how did companies manage to get the same work done?
luaChon: They hired temporary staff for busy periods.
They asked employees to work longer on the four days.
They bought software to do routine tasks.
They spent less time in meetings and reduced interruptions.
cau.giaiThich: Đoạn C: 'Meetings were made shorter or cancelled, and some firms introduced quiet hours in which nobody could be interrupted.' Thuê thêm người (A) là điều đoạn D nói bệnh viện sẽ phải làm — bẫy lấy chi tiết ở đoạn khác.

cau.de: What do critics say about the companies that took part in the trials?
luaChon: They were not typical, because they had volunteered.
They exaggerated their results.
They were paid to take part.
They were mostly very large firms.
cau.giaiThich: Đoạn D: 'the companies in such trials chose to take part, so they were probably the ones most likely to succeed.' chose to take part = volunteered ⇒ không đại diện cho mọi công ty. B, C, D không được nói.

cau.de: Why would a four-day week be difficult for a hospital?
luaChon: Its staff would refuse to change their hours.
It would have to employ extra people, which costs more.
Patients would complain about the service.
The law does not allow it to reduce hours.
cau.giaiThich: Đoạn D: 'A hospital or a restaurant cannot simply close for an extra day, and would need to hire more staff to cover the hours, which raises costs.' hire more staff = employ extra people; raises costs = costs more.

cau.de: Supporters say that workers who are ___ are more likely to make errors.
cau.giaiThich: Đoạn C: 'tired people make more mistakes and are ill more often.' mistakes = errors. Không điền ill: ill là hệ quả thứ hai của việc mệt, không phải nguyên nhân gây lỗi.

cau.de: Critics worry that a four-day week may put employees under more ___.
cau.giaiThich: Đoạn D: 'employees feeling under greater pressure to finish everything.' greater = more. under pressure = chịu áp lực.

cau.de: Working five shorter days is convenient for ___ who have children at school.
cau.giaiThich: Đoạn E: 'keep five days but shorten each of them. This suits parents, who can collect their children from school.' suits = is convenient for.
